title: Introduction to Automated Testing
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of introduction to automated testing using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates introduction to automated testing.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Introduction to Automated Testing** as part of **Testing, Debugging, Documentation, and Quality**. Reliable Kotlin code is supported by repeatable tests, meaningful assertions, debuggable failure reports, documentation, and review—not by coverage alone. Use the subtopics—Unit Testing Fundamentals, Tests, Fixtures, and Assertions, Test Naming and Organization—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Professional applications need repeatable tests, clear APIs, dependable dependencies, security checks, and observable failures. Apply this concept in small steps before integrating it into a larger project.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with unit testing fundamentals. Then compare it with tests, fixtures, and assertions. Identify the input, state, dependency, or branch that determines the result. The snippet is a static reference for CodeLeaf and is not executed in the lesson page.

items.title: Unit Testing Fundamentals
items.text: Unit Testing Fundamentals helps make behavior observable and repeatable. Define the expected result, include a boundary or failure case, and preserve enough diagnostic information to locate the cause without leaking sensitive data.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Introduction to Automated Testing removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
